steps.message:
Item 048 on our Package A register falls due on 07/20/2026, and the Block B plant-room excavation the Contractor has planned for 08/10/2026 cannot start until it is closed. I am taking it myself. Item 048 is the Kesterline shoring design for that excavation. Kesterline has since supplemented the sealed Rev.1 with Rev.2, sent under its letter KE-L-2026-0713, which is attached, and is asking for verification on that basis so that the excavation can go ahead. Verify the item on its current revision against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions.

Work it through against the project record and issue the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck, on the attached memorandum form, keeping its sections. Set out the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition; say which of the design's checks can be carried forward as they stand and which, if any, cannot; say what the excavation this item releases would do to the permanent work already built at Block B; say what has to be produced before the excavation can start and who has to produce it; and say what the disposition means for the 08/10/2026 excavation start. Give the register response you would record under my name, A. Vance, dated 07/20/2026, and the status the item should carry, closing it only if you have verified it. Save the memo as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx.

RW-B3, and RW-B4) shall be installed outside the sheet line at the four corners of the Block B pit. Each relief well shall be screened from El. 718.0

R2.2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 5)
With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined dense sand and gravel aquifer at El. 720.0, a 6.0 ft clay plug remains below
the excavation base. Base heave stability against artesian uplift is verified in accordance with DBM §6.2 at the controlled piezometric head of El.
726.5 (representing a piezometric head hw = 726.5 − 720.0 = 6.5 ft above the aquifer top at El. 720.0):
 Unfactored Clay Plug Weight (W): For the 6.0 ft clay plug at saturated unit weight γclay = 120 pcf:
W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf ⇒ W = 720 psf
 Factored Resisting Plug Weight (0.9W): Per DBM §6.2, applying the 0.90 resistance factor to total soil plug weight:
0.9W = 648 psf
 Controlled Upward Water Pressure (u): At the controlled confined head of El. 726.5 (γw = 62.4 pcf):
u = (726.5 − 720.0) ft × 62.4 pcf = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf ⇒ u = 405.6 psf
 Base Heave Factor of Safety:
FSheave = 0.9W / u = 648 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.60 (FS 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2 — OK)

The steel sheet-pile wall is embedded a depth of D = 6.5 ft below final excavation subgrade (El. 726.0) to a sheet-pile tip elevation of El. 719.5 (total

R2.1 — Groundwater Conditions, Relief Wells & Excavation Staging (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 3.4 & Part of Section 10)
The Rev.1 dry-excavation assumption is hereby formally withdrawn. For the Block B plant-room excavation (ground surface at El. 750.0, final
excavation subgrade at El. 726.0, exposed wall height H = 24.0 ft), the revised design groundwater and stratigraphy profile is established from
KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 and CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 as follows:
 Design Phreatic Water Table Behind Wall: El. 742.0 (shallow phreatic surface behind the sheet-pile wall, Geotechnical Report KGI-2024-0417
Rev.2, Section 7). The excavation side is drained to subgrade El. 726.0 by sumps within the sheeted pit.
 Confining Clay Aquitard: Stiff cohesive clay stratum extending from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 (18.0 ft total thickness, leaving a 6.0 ft clay plug
below final excavation subgrade El. 726.0).
 Confined Aquifer Top & Initial Piezometric Head: The top of the underlying confined dense sand and gravel (SW-GW) aquifer is located at El.
720.0, with an initial unpumped confined piezometric head at El. 738.0 (18.0 ft of artesian head above the aquifer top).
To depressurize the confined SW-GW aquifer prior to deep excavation, four 8-in diameter pressure-relief wells (designated RW-B1, RW-B2,
RW-B3, and RW-B4) shall be installed outside the sheet line at the four corners of the Block B pit. Each relief well shall be screened from El. 718.0

R2.2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 5)
With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined dense sand and gravel aquifer at El. 720.0, a 6.0 ft clay plug remains below
the excavation base. Base heave stability against artesian uplift is verified in accordance with DBM §6.2 at the controlled piezometric head of El.
726.5 (representing a piezometric head hw = 726.5 − 720.0 = 6.5 ft above the aquifer top at El. 720.0):
 Unfactored Clay Plug Weight (W): For the 6.0 ft clay plug at saturated unit weight γclay = 120 pcf:
W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf ⇒ W = 720 psf
 Factored Resisting Plug Weight (0.9W): Per DBM §6.2, applying the 0.90 resistance factor to total soil plug weight:
0.9W = 648 psf
 Controlled Upward Water Pressure (u): At the controlled confined head of El. 726.5 (γw = 62.4 pcf):
u = (726.5 − 720.0) ft × 62.4 pcf = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf ⇒ u = 405.6 psf
 Base Heave Factor of Safety:
FSheave = 0.9W / u = 648 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.60 (FS 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2 — OK)

R2.4 — Sheet-Pile Toe Embedment Check (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 6)
The steel sheet-pile wall is embedded a depth of D = 6.5 ft below final excavation subgrade (El. 726.0) to a sheet-pile tip elevation of El. 719.5 (total
sheet-pile length = 30.5 ft from El. 750.0 to El. 719.5; the toe is lowered from the Rev.1 tip elevation of El. 722.0, and Rev.1 Section 13.1, item 3 is
amended to the revised tip elevation). Below subgrade the wall is embedded in the CL clay aquitard, whose permeability is of the order of 10−8
cm/s, and the embedment is checked in the undrained condition using the total-stress net passive pressure formulation (U.S. Steel Sheet Piling
Design Manual, anchored bulkhead in clay). The retained side above subgrade is carried drained, with full water pressure, as the conservative
envelope. The revised 30.5 ft sheets are driven with the equipment of Rev.1 Section 11.3 (ICE 44B vibratory hammer with Delmag D19 finish),
which is adequate for the revised tip elevation.
Using the undrained shear strength su = 1,400 psf carried from Rev.1 Section 3.2 and the total overburden pressure σv0 = 3,106 psf at subgrade
El. 726.0 from Section R2.3, the uniform net passive resistance below subgrade is:
pn = 4su − σv0 = 4(1,400 psf) − 3,106 psf = 5,600 psf − 3,106 psf = 2,494.0 psf
Over the embedment depth D = 6.5 ft, the unfactored passive toe force and stabilizing moment about the ground anchor elevation at El. 745.5 are:
 Unfactored Passive Toe Resistance (Pp): Pp = 2,494.0 psf × 6.5 ft = 16,211 lb/ft acting at mid-embedment El. 722.75.
 Moment Arm About Anchor (El. 745.5): zp = 745.5 − 722.75 = 22.75 ft.
 Resisting Passive Moment (MR): MR = 16,211 lb/ft × 22.75 ft = 368,800 ft-lb/ft.
 Rotational Toe Factor of Safety: Against the driving moment of 237,293 ft-lb/ft from Section R2.3:
FStoe = MR / MD = 368,800 ft-lb/ft / 237,293 ft-lb/ft = 1.55 (FS 1.55 ≥ 1.50 required — OK)
The free-earth support formulation adopted presumes full mobilisation of the net passive resistance over the embedded length, consistent with the
anchored-bulkhead analysis of the U.S. Steel manual, and the factor of safety of 1.50 applied to the resisting moment covers the mobilisation
required.
At tip elevation El. 719.5, the sheet-pile toe extends 0.5 ft into the SW-GW stratum below El. 720.0 so that the tips bear below the base of the clay,
as contemplated in Geotechnical Report Section 9.4. The penetration is nominal and the sheet-pile wall is not credited as a cutoff against
confined aquifer flow; the aquifer is continuous beneath the pit and is controlled by the relief wells of R2.1, and the sheet interlocks are sealed over
the aquitard interval in accordance with Geotechnical Report Section 9.6.

R2.5 — Tieback Ground Anchor Design (Continued)
 Design Anchor Load at 6 ft Centres: Crediting the allowable passive toe resistance (Pp,allow = 16,211 / 1.50 = 10,807 lb/ft) against the total
horizontal driving load of 19,610 lb/ft (Section R2.3), the required horizontal anchor reaction is Th = 19,610 − 10,807 = 8,803 lb/ft. For anchors
spaced at 6 ft centres and inclined at 20° below horizontal, the design anchor working load is:
Tdesign = (8,803 lb/ft × 6.0 ft) / cos 20° = 52,818 lb / 0.93969 = 56,208 lb = 56.2 kips
 Anchor Bond Capacity: The 24 ft bond length is formed by pressure-grouted tieback installation through a 6.0-in nominal diameter drill hole
(dh = 6.0 in) at the design bond stress of 20 psi adopted in Rev.1 Section 10.4 (FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). Temporary drill casing is advanced
and grouted over the aquitard interval to seal against artesian seepage during anchor installation. Ultimate bond capacity is:
Qult = π × dh × Lb × τbond = π × 6.0 in × (24 ft × 12 in/ft) × 20 psi = 108,573 lb = 108.6 kips
 Anchor Capacity Check: Comparing ultimate bond capacity of 108.6 kips against the design load of 56.2 kips at 6 ft centres yields a factor of
safety of FSanchor = 108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93 (adequate on the adopted design bond stress of FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). The anchor tendon is
unchanged from Rev.1 Section 10.1: (4) 0.6-in Grade 270 strand, design strength 140 kips against the 56.2 kip design load. Each anchor is
proof tested to 1.33 × 56.2 = 74.8 kips and locked off at 0.75 × 56.2 = 42.2 kips. The proof load exceeds the design load by 33 per cent and is
taken as the demonstration of anchor performance for the period the wall is in service.

The PZ-35 Grade 50 section adopted in Rev.1 Section 11.2 is retained and re-checked against the revised effective-stress plus hydrostatic lateral
loading (Fy = 50 ksi, elastic section modulus Sx = 48.5 in3/ft of wall).
 Allowable Flexural Capacity (Mallow): At an allowable bending stress of Fb = 0.60 Fy = 30.0 ksi per AISC 360-16 Chapter F, as adopted in
Rev.1 Section 11.2:
Mallow = (Fb × Sx) / (12 in/ft) = (30.0 ksi × 48.5 in3/ft) / 12 = 121 kip-ft/ft
 Maximum Span Bending Moment (Mmax): Under the Section R2.3 loading and El. 745.5 anchor reaction, the point of zero shear occurs at El.
733.1, producing a maximum flexural demand of 62.4 kip-ft/ft.
 Flexural Factor of Safety: FSflex = 121 kip-ft/ft / 62.4 kip-ft/ft = 1.94 ≥ 1.50 required (Rev.1 §11.2) (PZ-35 Grade 50 section is structurally
adequate).

2. Executive Summary
Construction on Package A during June 2026 continued to track the current baseline schedule to within a
nominal variance. The Contractor completed the Level-2 suspended slab placements (Sets 1 through 5, dated
05/18/2026 through 06/05/2026) and rolled cage prefabrication for the Level-3 slab into the site's rebar yard.
Level-2 concrete cylinders cast during the reporting period were on the 28-day break curve at the Vantree
laboratory; the last of the June 28-day breaks (Set 4) was tested 06/29/2026, and Set 5 remains to be broken
07/03/2026 with the report packet consolidated shortly thereafter.
The next contractual hold-point is the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 at 0530. All open Package A
verifications on the Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register are required-by 07/20/2026 so that
the pour is not released without written verification. The pre-pour reinforcement and cover inspection is
scheduled for 07/13/2026; the Level-3 rebar lot is expected to arrive on 07/10/2026 for tagging and traceability
review.
Beyond the July 22 pour, the next material milestone is the start of the Block B plant-room excavation on
08/10/2026. The delegated shoring design (Rev.1 resubmittal 06/11/2026) is under review, together with the
associated dewatering and groundwater control documentation.
No lost-time incidents were reported in June. Weather losses were within the schedule contingency. The
Owner's contingency has not been drawn against during the period.

5.4 Groundwater Monitoring
Kelbrook Geotechnical continued the Package A piezometer monitoring program. The 06/28/2026 reading was
the 19th in the series that began 11/22/2024. Shallow standpipes read El. 741.6 to El. 742.4 ft; deep piezometers

maximum of 0.61 in at the most-loaded monitored footing. The rate is being tracked against the 1.0 in total / 0.5
in differential tolerance in Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6. Data are compiled in the Foundation Settlement
Monitoring log for Block C and are carried in the geotechnical serviceability verification, Item 051.

SECTION 1 — DESIGN BASIS
1.1 General
These calculations establish the design of the temporary support of excavation for the deep plant-room excavation
planned beneath Block B of Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program. The excavation is a
rectangular pit approximately 68 ft × 44 ft in plan, cut into the podium footprint east of the shared Block A/B
basement. Excavation commences from a working grade at El. 750.0 and terminates at a plant-room subgrade at
El. 726.0, a total excavated depth of 24 ft.
The temporary works described herein are the Contractor's means and methods and are supplied by delegated
1.2 Selected System
A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
 (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
 (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
 (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
lagging.
Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

This dewatering plan addresses dewatering of the Block A basement excavation only, to subgrade El. 730.0
approximate. It does NOT extend to the separate deep excavation planned beneath Block B, which will be
addressed by a separate delegated design.

within the Block B enclosure will be managed by sump control of surface and construction water only. The Block

compressible clay stratum (toe at El. 722.0), covered under a separate submittal.

site (see Part 4 — Limitations);

carried under a separate submittal package by others.

the compressible clay aquitard, will require a separately-sealed dewatering and groundwater control analysis.

safety against base heave; and (d) whether relief of the confined head, by means outside the scope of this
submittal (e.g., deep relief wells screened in the sand and gravel), is required to establish an adequate factor of

3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

8.3  Downdrag on Deep Foundations
The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients
measured in the laboratory series, is expected to continue for a period measured in years rather than
months.
Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.
Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
Section 9.3.

Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of

Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation

2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
Section 6 of the reference report:
 From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
structural fill re-use.
 From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
 From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent

excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)

4. Seepage Observations — Block A Excavation and Dewatering Response
4.1 Seepage into the Cut Face
During the Block A basement excavation, groundwater seepage was observed entering the excavation at the
exposed cut face where the upper SP-SM sand was cut below the design water table. Seepage was concentrated
at elevations El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, corresponding to the top of the phreatic surface in the upper sand. The
seepage was clear (non-turbid after brief initial flushing), sustained rather than intermittent, and distributed
along the cut face rather than emerging from a discrete conduit or seam. No seepage was observed emerging
from the top of the CL clay at El. 738.0; the clay presented no visible cracks or fissures and no seepage exit
points at or below its exposed face.
The observed seepage elevations (El. 741.8 to El. 742.2) reproduce the range recorded in exploratory
test-pitting during the original 2024 investigation and are consistent with the shallow standpipe piezometer
readings from stations outside the dewatered footprint (Section 3.1). The two independent measurements —
piezometer standpipe readings and cut-face seepage entry — corroborate each other and confirm the design
water table elevation.

4.2 Well-Point Dewatering Response — Upper Sand
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
was operated continuously across the Block A footprint from 07/12/2025 through the mat placement
date and beyond. Piezometer readings taken from a spare standpipe drop set inside the dewatered perimeter, in
combination with well-point riser inspections, showed the upper sand water level drawn down to approximately
El. 728 within the dewatered perimeter — approximately 14 feet below the ambient design water table and
approximately 2 feet below the working subgrade at El. 730.0. Drawdown within the perimeter was achieved
within approximately 48 hours of well-point activation and was maintained at that level throughout the
excavation and mat construction window.
The dewatering system performed as designed for the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand across the
Block A footprint. Cut faces below the ambient water table, once well-point drawdown was established,
presented no free seepage during the balance of the mat construction sequence.
4.3 Deep Piezometer Response — Confirms Confined Aquifer Independence
Deep piezometer readings from B-04 and B-08 (both screened in the deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 and
located within the Block A / Block B footprint) were taken throughout the Block A dewatering campaign.
Across the full period of well-point operation, both deep piezometers continued to read within the range El.
737.7 to El. 738.3, with individual monthly means at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0.
Deep piezometer readings within the Block A footprint were unaffected by upper-sand well-point dewatering.
The upper sand and the deep aquifer are separated by the 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to
El. 720.0, and the well-point system draws only from the upper sand. The observed independence of the two
regimes during active dewatering directly confirms the confined character of the deep aquifer and the aquitard
behaviour of the clay, as characterized in the reference report.

3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

Adrian —

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. I would appreciate a short written status against each item by end of day 07/20/2026 so that Steven and Gregory have a clean picture before the 07/22/2026 hold-point is either released or moved. If it is easier to walk me through it beforehand, I am available Monday afternoon.

Thank you.

Rachel

To depressurize the confined SW-GW aquifer prior to deep excavation, four 8-in diameter pressure-relief wells (designated RW-B1, RW-B2,
RW-B3, and RW-B4) shall be installed outside the sheet line at the four corners of the Block B pit. Each relief well shall be screened from El. 718.0

R2.2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 5)
With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined dense sand and gravel aquifer at El. 720.0, a 6.0 ft clay plug remains below
the excavation base. Base heave stability against artesian uplift is verified in accordance with DBM §6.2 at the controlled piezometric head of El.
726.5 (representing a piezometric head hw = 726.5 − 720.0 = 6.5 ft above the aquifer top at El. 720.0):
 Unfactored Clay Plug Weight (W): For the 6.0 ft clay plug at saturated unit weight γclay = 120 pcf:
W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf ⇒ W = 720 psf
 Factored Resisting Plug Weight (0.9W): Per DBM §6.2, applying the 0.90 resistance factor to total soil plug weight:
0.9W = 648 psf
 Controlled Upward Water Pressure (u): At the controlled confined head of El. 726.5 (γw = 62.4 pcf):
u = (726.5 − 720.0) ft × 62.4 pcf = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf ⇒ u = 405.6 psf
 Base Heave Factor of Safety:
FSheave = 0.9W / u = 648 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.60 (FS 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2 — OK)

The steel sheet-pile wall is embedded a depth of D = 6.5 ft below final excavation subgrade (El. 726.0) to a sheet-pile tip elevation of El. 719.5 (total
sheet-pile length = 30.5 ft from El. 750.0 to El. 719.5; the toe is lowered from the Rev.1 tip elevation of El. 722.0, and Rev.1 Section 13.1, item 3 is

Design Manual, anchored bulkhead in clay). The retained side above subgrade is carried drained, with full water pressure, as the conservative
envelope. The revised 30.5 ft sheets are driven with the equipment of Rev.1 Section 11.3 (ICE 44B vibratory hammer with Delmag D19 finish),

Using the undrained shear strength su = 1,400 psf carried from Rev.1 Section 3.2 and the total overburden pressure σv0 = 3,106 psf at subgrade
El. 726.0 from Section R2.3, the uniform net passive resistance below subgrade is:
pn = 4su − σv0 = 4(1,400 psf) − 3,106 psf = 5,600 psf − 3,106 psf = 2,494.0 psf
Over the embedment depth D = 6.5 ft, the unfactored passive toe force and stabilizing moment about the ground anchor elevation at El. 745.5 are:
 Unfactored Passive Toe Resistance (Pp): Pp = 2,494.0 psf × 6.5 ft = 16,211 lb/ft acting at mid-embedment El. 722.75.

PART 4 — LIMITATIONS
4.1 Confined Aquifer
Because the confined aquifer at El. 720.0 is separated from the upper sand by the CL aquitard El. 738.0 to El.
720.0, dewatering by perimeter well points in the upper sand will not reduce the confined head. The confined
piezometric head at El. 738.0 is developed in the deep sand and gravel below El. 720.0 and is sustained by a
source of recharge that is hydraulically decoupled from the shallow phreatic surface targeted by this system.
Any excavation extending toward or into the confined aquifer will require separate analysis. Such analysis shall
address, at minimum: (a) the residual thickness of the clay aquitard beneath the excavation subgrade; (b) the
weight of that residual plug relative to the confined uplift acting on its underside at El. 720.0; (c) the factor of
safety against base heave; and (d) whether relief of the confined head, by means outside the scope of this
submittal (e.g., deep relief wells screened in the sand and gravel), is required to establish an adequate factor of
safety.
Nothing in this submittal has been designed to, and nothing in this submittal shall be construed to, relieve the
confined piezometric head.
4.2 Adjacent and Subsequent Work
This plan is limited to the Block A basement excavation defined in Article 1.2. It shall not be relied upon by
others as the basis for:
(a) Design of temporary shoring outside the Block A footprint;
(b) Design of excavation support, cofferdams or cutoff walls beneath Block B or elsewhere on the site;
(c) Any calculation that treats the excavation as dry, dewatered or relieved outside the extents shown in Article
3.2 above;
(d) Any design that assumes a reduction in the confined piezometric head below El. 738.0 at any location.
Any delegated design outside the Block A basement footprint shall independently verify the groundwater
conditions applicable to that work directly from the Geotechnical Report or from a separately-sealed
hydrogeologic evaluation. The undersigned engineer's seal below applies only to the temporary works described
in this submittal, within the scope defined in Article 1.2, and only for the Block A basement excavation.
4.3 Duration
This plan is prepared for the temporary construction duration of the Block A below-grade work. It does not
constitute a permanent groundwater control system and does not address long-term dewatering. Permanent
below-grade water management for the completed structure is addressed under separate design by the Architect
of Record and Structural Engineer of Record (below-grade waterproofing and drainage details, see Package A
architectural and structural documents).
4.4 Weather and Recharge
The upper sand phreatic surface in the vicinity of the excavation may respond to seasonal recharge from
significant precipitation events. The 25% reserve pump capacity provided under Article 3.2 is intended to
accommodate ordinary seasonal fluctuation. Extraordinary precipitation events (e.g., a 10-year 24-hour event)
may require additional temporary measures to be added by the Contractor.

1.2 Selected System
A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
 (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
 (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
 (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
lagging.
Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

1. Purpose and Scope
This field observation report documents excavation observations, groundwater monitoring readings and seepage
observations recorded by Kelbrook Geotechnical field personnel across the Package A footprint over the
construction period 07/2025 through 05/2026. The observations reported herein are drawn from the writer’s
daily field notes, from the shallow standpipe and deep piezometer monitoring log maintained under the ongoing
Package A groundwater monitoring program, and from photographs and sketches taken at the time of
observation. The report is furnished in support of the Owner’s Representative construction verification file and
as supplemental record to the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417).
Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of
2025 to a working subgrade at approximately El. 730.0; and (b) the placement of engineered fill across the
Block B footprint from 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 and the subsequent months of pile installation and
lift-up to design grade. Groundwater monitoring is continuous across both episodes and is reported in full.

2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression

Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A

Page 1

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.

Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528

The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on
07/14/2025 and progressed from existing grade El. 750.0 down to a working subgrade at approximately El.
730.0 (approximately one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5, to accommodate a
lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.

2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
Section 6 of the reference report:
•

From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
structural fill re-use.

•

From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.

•

From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.

The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.

2.3 Working Subgrade Condition
Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.
Marcus Whitfield) and the Owner’s Representative (Mr. Adrian Vance
). Subgrade was found to be firm,
uniform, free of standing water within the dewatered footprint, and suitable to receive the lean-concrete
working mat and subsequently the reinforced mat foundation. No soft spots, disturbed zones or unsuitable
inclusions were logged. The subgrade approval memorandum was issued separately by Kelbrook on
08/07/2025.

3. Groundwater Monitoring — Continuous Record
Groundwater monitoring under the Package A program continues from the piezometer array installed
11/22/2024 and reported in the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2. Over the observation period 07/2025
through 05/2026 an additional eleven monitoring rounds were completed, bringing the total record to eighteen

rounds since installation. Readings are taken monthly (weekly during active excavation and dewatering).

Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A

Page 2

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.

Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528

3.1 Design Water Table — Upper Sand (Shallow Standpipe Piezometers)
The design water table in the upper SP-SM sand, established at El. 742.0 in the reference report, is confirmed
by the extended monitoring record. Readings from the three shallow standpipe piezometers (B-01, B-03, B-09),
taken across the 07/2025 through 05/2026 observation period at locations outside the Block A dewatered
footprint, remain in the range El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, with individual monthly means clustered within a few
tenths of a foot of El. 742.0. No systematic trend, no seasonal excursion beyond that range and no departure
from the design elevation was recorded.

3.2 Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer (Deep Piezometers)
The confined piezometric head in the deep SW-GW sand-and-gravel aquifer below El. 720.0, established at El.
738.0 in the reference report, is likewise confirmed. Readings from the two deep piezometers (B-04 and B-08),
both screened below El. 720.0 within the Block B footprint, remain in the range El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across
the full extended record. The head is stable, without trend, and consistent with the value carried forward from
the Rev.2 investigation.

Both regimes — the shallow phreatic surface at El. 742.0 in the upper sands and the confined piezometric head
at El. 738.0 in the deep aquifer below El. 720.0 — remain consistent with KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2. The
eighteen-foot separation between the top of the clay aquitard and the top of the deep aquifer continues to isolate
the two regimes.

4. Seepage Observations — Block A Excavation and Dewatering Response
4.1 Seepage into the Cut Face
During the Block A basement excavation, groundwater seepage was observed entering the excavation at the
exposed cut face where the upper SP-SM sand was cut below the design water table. Seepage was concentrated
at elevations El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, corresponding to the top of the phreatic surface in the upper sand. The
seepage was clear (non-turbid after brief initial flushing), sustained rather than intermittent, and distributed
along the cut face rather than emerging from a discrete conduit or seam. No seepage was observed emerging
from the top of the CL clay at El. 738.0; the clay presented no visible cracks or fissures and no seepage exit
points at or below its exposed face.
The observed seepage elevations (El. 741.8 to El. 742.2) reproduce the range recorded in exploratory
test-pitting during the original 2024 investigation and are consistent with the shallow standpipe piezometer
readings from stations outside the dewatered footprint (Section 3.1). The two independent measurements —
piezometer standpipe readings and cut-face seepage entry — corroborate each other and confirm the design
water table elevation.

Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A

Page 3

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.

Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528

4.2 Well-Point Dewatering Response — Upper Sand
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
was operated continuously across the Block A footprint from 07/12/2025 through the mat placement
date and beyond. Piezometer readings taken from a spare standpipe drop set inside the dewatered perimeter, in
combination with well-point riser inspections, showed the upper sand water level drawn down to approximately
El. 728 within the dewatered perimeter — approximately 14 feet below the ambient design water table and
approximately 2 feet below the working subgrade at El. 730.0. Drawdown within the perimeter was achieved
within approximately 48 hours of well-point activation and was maintained at that level throughout the
excavation and mat construction window.
The dewatering system performed as designed for the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand across the
Block A footprint. Cut faces below the ambient water table, once well-point drawdown was established,
presented no free seepage during the balance of the mat construction sequence.

4.3 Deep Piezometer Response — Confirms Confined Aquifer Independence
Deep piezometer readings from B-04 and B-08 (both screened in the deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 and
located within the Block A / Block B footprint) were taken throughout the Block A dewatering campaign.
Across the full period of well-point operation, both deep piezometers continued to read within the range El.
737.7 to El. 738.3, with individual monthly means at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0.
Deep piezometer readings within the Block A footprint were unaffected by upper-sand well-point dewatering.
The upper sand and the deep aquifer are separated by the 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to
El. 720.0, and the well-point system draws only from the upper sand. The observed independence of the two
regimes during active dewatering directly confirms the confined character of the deep aquifer and the aquitard
behaviour of the clay, as characterized in the reference report.

5. Notes on Block B — Engineered Fill Placement and Subsequent Monitoring
5.1 Engineered Fill Placement, 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025
Engineered fill was placed across the Block B footprint over the period 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 to bring
the site from natural ground at approximately El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0 — a nominal 12 ft of fill
in 14 controlled lifts. Fill was placed directly on the stripped clay surface after removal of the surface topsoil
mantle, in accordance with the recommendations of Section 9.5 of the reference report. Compaction and
moisture control were performed under the independent Laboratory’s field density testing program (Vantree
Materials Testing, LLC); the writer’s observations here are limited to the geotechnical monitoring associated
with the underlying strata.

5.2 Deep Piezometer Readings Through Fill Placement, Pile Driving and Subsequent Months
The two deep piezometers B-04 and B-08 are located within the Block B footprint (B-04 within the plant-room
excavation footprint, B-08 adjacent to the basement mat perimeter beneath Blocks A and B, both screened in
the deep aquifer below El. 720.0). Both remained instrumented and readable through fill placement, through
pile installation from 11/06/2025 through 11/21/2025, and through the subsequent months of the observation
period.
Across the entire sequence — before, during and after fill placement; before, during and after pile driving; and
through the months following pile driving — deep piezometer readings continued to fall within the range El.
737.7 to El. 738.3. Individual monthly means remained clustered at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0. No
pumping, no departure from the ambient range, and no sustained response either to fill loading or to pile

Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A

Page 4

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.

Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528

installation was recorded in the deep-aquifer piezometers.
The aquifer head re-establishes at El. 738.0 through the engineered fill placed above the clay; the fill does not
alter the confined head, and the confined head does not respond to the fill load. This is expected behaviour for a
laterally continuous confined aquifer isolated from the surface loading regime by an intact clay aquitard, and is
reported here so that the record is complete.

5.3 Shallow Standpipe Readings
Shallow standpipe piezometer B-01 (Block A, outside the Block B fill footprint) and B-09 (Block C, outside the
Block B fill footprint) continued to read within the El. 741.6 to El. 742.4 range through the fill-placement and
pile-driving windows. Shallow standpipe B-03 (Block A / Block B transition) likewise continued in that range.
The upper-sand phreatic surface at El. 742.0 outside the Block A dewatered footprint was not measurably
affected by activity within the Block B fill footprint.

6. Field Observation Summary
The following observations are recorded for the observation period 07/2025 through 05/2026:
1. The Block A basement excavation was opened in summer 2025 and carried to a working subgrade at

8. ENGINEERING ANALYSIS
8.1 Consolidation of the Clay Aquitard
The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard is normally-consolidated (Section 5.2). Any net stress increase q applied at
the top of the clay will produce virgin, one-dimensional consolidation settlement along the Cc slope. In terms of
the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
Sc

= Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]

with:
• Cc = 0.28
• e0 = 0.92
• H (thickness of clay) = 18 ft
• σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth of clay (El. 729)
For any q > (σ'p − σ'0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin compression governs and the above expression applies. Because σ'p is
only marginally above σ'0, this threshold is exceeded by essentially any structural or fill load of engineering
interest.
The engineering consequences discussed in Sections 8.3 and 9 flow directly from this. Two q scenarios are of
particular importance at Package A:
• Fill surcharge on Block B. Placement of engineered fill from El. 738.0 up to El. 750.0 (nominal 12 ft) at
Block B applies q ≈ 12 · (γfill − γw_avg) at depth (with an unfactored gross fill weight on the order of

must compute the resulting long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement using the parameters

8.3 Downdrag on Deep Foundations

The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients
measured in the laboratory series, is expected to continue for a period measured in years rather than
months.
Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.
Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
Section 9.3.

['Scope', '']
['Vantree Materials Testing, LLC ("Vantree" or "the Laboratory") was contracted to the Owner, Thornbury State University, to perform geotechnical laboratory index testing on samples recovered by Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. from Borings B-01 through B-09 drilled at the Package A site during the field exploration period 10/28/2024 through 11/22/2024. Samples were received under chain-of-custody on 11/25/2024, logged in as project VMT-2024-0917-PkgA-INDEX, and stored at the Laboratory\'s climate-controlled sample room until testing. The results are presented in the INDEX TESTS sheet, with Package A design unit weights compiled in the SUMMARY sheet.', '']
['ASTM test methods', '']
['The following ASTM standards apply to the tests reported in this workbook:', '']
['Method', 'Title']
['ASTM D422', 'Standard Test Method for Particle-Size Analysis of Soils (grain-size distribution; sieve and hydrometer)']
['ASTM D4318', 'Standard Test Methods for Liquid Limit, Plastic Limit, and Plasticity Index of Soils (Atterberg limits)']
['ASTM D2216', 'Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass']
['ASTM D854', 'Standard Test Methods for Specific Gravity of Soil Solids by Water Pycnometer']
['ASTM D7263', 'Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Density (Unit Weight) of Soil Specimens']
['ASTM D2487', 'Standard Practice for Classification of Soils for Engineering Purposes (Unified Soil Classification System) — used to assign USCS group symbols']
['Grain-size distributions in the INDEX TESTS sheet were determined in accordance with ASTM D422. Atterberg limits (LL, PL, PI) were determined in accordance with ASTM D4318, Method A (multipoint liquid-limit method) for the cohesive samples; the granular SP-SM and SW-GW samples are non-plastic (NP) as determined by the plastic-limit test in accordance with ASTM D4318. Natural moisture contents were determined on the recovered field mass in accordance with ASTM D2216. Specific gravity of solids was determined on representative fines in accordance with ASTM D854. Total (moist) unit weight was determined on trimmed sub-specimens of the thin-walled Shelby-tube samples in accordance with ASTM D7263.', '']
['Sample inventory', '']
["Samples tested comprise (a) recovered split-spoon (SPT) sub-samples from all nine borings for classification, moisture and grain-size analysis, and (b) thin-walled Shelby-tube (undisturbed) sub-specimens from the clay aquitard for unit-weight determination. The Shelby-tube samples designated B-04 U-1, B-06 U-1, B-06 U-2, B-06 U3, B-08 U-1, and B-08 U2 were received. Of these, B-06 U3 and B-08 U2 were also forwarded to the Laboratory's consolidation test bench for ASTM D2435 one-dimensional consolidation testing; the D2435 results are reported separately in workbook Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx (Vantree Laboratory Report No. VMT-2025-0109-CON). Trimmings from B-06 U3 and B-08 U2 were retained for the index tests reported herein so that the soil classification and Atterberg limits are common between the two reports. Natural moisture content and density were determined independently on each test bench, on separate trimmings taken at different levels within the tube, and are reported as measured by each; the unit weights tabulated herein are the values furnished for design use in the stratum.", '']

['Basis of design unit weights', '', '', '', '']
['Upper sand (SP-SM), 118 pcf.', '', '', '', '']
['The upper sand exists in two states within the Package A profile: (i) moist medium-dense above the phreatic surface at El. 742.0, with in-situ moisture 10 to 13% from the D2216 measurements, and (ii) saturated below El. 742.0 down to the contact with the CL clay at El. 738.0, with moisture 18 to 22%. The design total unit weight of 118 pcf represents an average moist-plus-saturated bulk condition appropriate for the Package A upper-sand thickness (approximately El. 750.0 down to El. 738.0 net of stripped topsoil / fill).', '', '', '', '']
['Clay aquitard (CL), 120 pcf.', '', '', '', '']
['The design total unit weight of 120 pcf is the average of the six ASTM D7263 determinations on the undisturbed Shelby-tube samples across the aquitard thickness. Individual specimen determinations clustered tightly and are reported as 120 pcf in the INDEX TESTS sheet for all six specimens. Atterberg limits (LL ≈ 40, PL ≈ 19, PI ≈ 21) indicate medium plasticity, consistent with the D2487 CL classification. Natural moistures 24 to 28% and Gs = 2.72 place the in-situ void ratio in the range consistent with normally-consolidated stratigraphy.', '', '', '', '']
['Dense sand and gravel (SW-GW), 130 pcf.', '', '', '', '']
['The confined aquifer material below El. 720.0 was recovered as disturbed split-spoon material only (SPT refusal encountered on penetration); undisturbed sampling was not attempted. The 130 pcf design total unit weight is a conservative correlation from grain-size, D854 specific gravity (2.68), and moisture (7 to 9%) consistent with dense to very dense well-graded sand and gravel of the type recovered.', '', '', '', '']

PART 1

GENERAL

1.1 SUMMARY
A. Section Includes:
1. Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.

Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.

3. Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4. Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B. Related Sections:
1.

Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.

2. Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3. Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2 REFERENCES
A.

Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.

ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.

2.

ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.

3. ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.

ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content

 when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5. ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3 DEFINITIONS
A.

Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.

B. Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.

Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.

D.

Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.

E.

Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.

1.4 QUALITY ASSURANCE
A. Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.

Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.

C.

Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.

1.5 SUBMITTALS
A. Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.

Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.

2.

Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.

PART 2

PRODUCTS

2.1 STRUCTURAL FILL
A.

Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.

B.

Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.

C.

Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.

D.

Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.

2.2 COMMON FILL
A. Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3 CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A. Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.

PART 3

EXECUTION

3.1 EXAMINATION
A.

Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.

3.2 SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A. Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B. Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present

 to witness the proof roll.
C.

Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.

3.3 PLACEMENT
A. Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.

Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.

C.

Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.

D.

Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.

3.4 COMPACTION
A. Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B. Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.

Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.

The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.

2.

Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

3.5 BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A. Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.

B.

Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.

C. Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.

A.

Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.

constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.

C.

Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.

3.7 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A. Testing frequency for structural fill:
1. In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.

Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.

B.

Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.

C.

Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

SECTION 8 — SLIDING AND OVERTURNING CHECK
8.1 Sliding
The wall does not translate horizontally as a rigid body because it is restrained by the tieback anchor at El. 745.5
(see Section 10) and by the passive block below subgrade. The tieback horizontal reaction (15.4 kips/ft, per
Section 7.3) is the direct restraint against horizontal translation of the upper wall; the passive block restrains
translation of the toe. Sliding is therefore not a rigid-body failure mode for this wall configuration; the applicable
checks are the anchor pull-out (Section 10) and the toe embedment (Section 9).
For completeness, and treating the sheet-pile section conservatively as a floating rigid strip with only the passive
block available for restraint (i.e., without any tieback contribution), the sliding factor of safety is:
FS_sliding = P_p / P_A = 3,740 / (17,844 − 4,120 − 332)

This is the "wall-free" sliding number and confirms that the tieback is essential to global stability. With the
tieback engaged (Section 10), sliding is fully restrained.

        print(f"[Section {s_idx}] Header: {hdr} | Footer: {ftr}")
    for i, p in enumerate(doc.paragraphs):
        sname = p.style.name if p.style else "None"
        if p.text.strip():
            print(f"[P{i} ({sname})]: {p.text}")
    for ti, t in enumerate(doc.tables):
        print(f"\n--- Table {ti} ({len(t.rows)}x{len(t.columns)}) ---")
        for ri, row in enumerate(t.rows):
            vals = [c.text.strip().replace('\n', ' | ') for c in row.cells]
            print(f"Row {ri}: {vals}")

[P26 (None)]: 3.1 Logged Subsurface Stratigraphy and Soil Parameters (KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 §§5.2, 6.1–6.4, Tables 5-1 & 6-1; Boring Logs B-04, B-06, B-07, B-08; Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx; CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 §3): At the Block B footprint (originally a surface-drainage low at natural grade ~El. 738.0 where the upper SP-SM sand present at Blocks A and C is absent), 12.0 ft of compacted granular structural fill (SM / SP-SM) was placed in 14 lifts from El. 738.0 to working grade El. 750.0 between 10/06/2025 and 11/02/2025 (γ_total = 118 pcf, φ' = 32°, c' = 0, Ka = 0.3073, Kp = 3.25). Directly beneath the fill lies Stratum 2, an 18.0-ft-thick normally-consolidated, medium-plasticity lean clay aquitard (CL) from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 (γ_total = 120 pcf, permeability k ≈ 10^-8 cm/s, Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045, e0 = 0.92, σ'0 = 1,850 psf, σ'p = 1,900 psf, OCR = 1.03; drained parameters φ' = 26°, c' = 100 psf, Ka = 0.3905, Kp = 2.56). Critically, per KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 §6.3 (p. 13), the logged undrained shear strength of the CL clay aquitard interpreted from field vane and unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial testing on companion Shelby-tube samples is su = 900 to 1,100 psf (mean 1,000 psf). Below El. 720.0 (explored to El. 648.2 in B-04) lies Stratum 3, a very dense well-graded sand and gravel confined aquifer (SW-GW, γ_total = 130 pcf, SPT refusal N ≥ 50 blows/6 in).

[P31 (None)]: 4.  FINDINGS
[P32 (None)]: Finding 1 — Withdrawal of Dry-Excavation Assumption, Groundwater Basis, Relief-Well Depressurization & Piezometer Hold (Rev.1 §3.4 & §10 Superseded by Supplement §R2.1 & §R2.7 — VERIFIED IN PRINCIPLE, CONTINGENT ON SEALED BLOCK B DEWATERING SUBMITTAL): In Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 (§2 p. 5, §3.4 p. 6, §4.3 p. 7, §14.3(a) p. 20), Kesterline assumed a dry excavation from El. 750.0 to El. 726.0 based on Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1. That assumption violated Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 Articles 1.2 and 4.2 (pp. 2, 7), which limit well-point dewatering to Block A and forbid assuming dry conditions or confined head reduction below El. 738.0 outside Block A. In Supplement KE-L-2026-0713 §R2.1 (pp. 1–2), Kesterline withdraws the dry-excavation assumption and adopts the logged groundwater profile: shallow phreatic surface at El. 742.0 behind the wall (with pit sumps controlling interior water to subgrade El. 726.0), CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 (6.0 ft plug below El. 726.0), and confined SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 at initial head El. 738.0. To depressurize the confined aquifer, §R2.1 specifies four 8-in relief wells (RW-B1 to RW-B4) outside the four corners of the sheet-pile pit, screened El. 718.0 to El. 705.0 in the SW-GW aquifer with a continuous annular bentonite-cement grout seal from El. 721.0 to El. 738.0 across the clay aquitard (satisfying KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 §9.6), actively pumped to hold confined piezometric head ≤ El. 726.5 (11.5 ft drawdown) until the plant-room slab is cast. Three vibrating-wire piezometers (VW-B1 to VW-B3, tips at El. 719.0) inside the Block B footprint enforce a mandatory 72-hour confirmation hold (head ≤ El. 726.5) before excavating below El. 732.0, paired with an active stop-work trigger at El. 727.0 (§R2.7, p. 4). The hydrogeologic basis and depressurization criteria in §R2.1 and §R2.7 are consistent with the project record and can be carried forward, subject to submission of a separately sealed Block B dewatering plan (Submittal 31-DW-B or 31-DW-A Rev.2) and Ohio EPA NPDES permit documentation.
[P33 (None)]: Finding 2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification Against Confined Uplift (Rev.1 §5 Superseded by Supplement §R2.2 — VERIFIED AND CARRIED FORWARD AS IT STANDS): With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined SW-GW aquifer at El. 720.0 (KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 §6.1 Table 6-1, p. 12; Boring Logs B-04 p. 7 & B-06 p. 9), a residual clay plug of thickness t_plug = 726.0 − 720.0 = 6.0 ft remains below subgrade. At the logged clay total unit weight γ_clay = 120 pcf (Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx SUMMARY tab; KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 Table 5-1, p. 11), the unfactored vertical plug weight is W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf = 720.0 psf, and the factored resisting dead weight per CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 §6.2 (p. 6, ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6)) is 0.9W = 0.90 × 720.0 = 648.0 psf.
• Unpumped Condition (Logged Confined Head El. 738.0): Artesian head above El. 720.0 is h_w = 738.0 − 720.0 = 18.0 ft, producing upward pressure u_unpumped = 18.0 ft × 62.4 pcf = 1,123.2 psf. This yields FS_heave = 0.9W / u = 648.0 / 1,123.2 = 0.58 < 1.0 (unfactored W / u = 720.0 / 1,123.2 = 0.64 < 1.0), confirming catastrophic base heave/blowout without aquifer depressurization (as warned in KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 §§8.2 & 9.4, pp. 15, 18).
• Controlled Depressurized Condition (Head Held ≤ El. 726.5 per §R2.1): Artesian head above El. 720.0 is h_w = 726.5 − 720.0 = 6.5 ft, producing upward water pressure u = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf = 405.6 psf. This yields FS_heave = 0.9W / u = 648.0 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.598 ≈ 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 §6.2 (unfactored W / u = 720.0 / 405.6 = 1.78). Even at the §R2.7 stop-work trigger elevation of El. 727.0 (h_w = 7.0 ft, u = 436.8 psf), 0.9W / u = 648.0 / 436.8 = 1.48 (unfactored W / u = 1.65), preserving a positive stability margin. Supplement §R2.2 (p. 3) is mathematically verified and can be carried forward as it stands.

excavation subgrade at El. 726.0, exposed wall height H = 24.0 ft), the revised design groundwater and stratigraphy profile is established from

Design Manual, anchored bulkhead in clay). The retained side above subgrade is carried drained, with full water pressure, as the conservative

1.1 General
These calculations establish the design of the temporary support of excavation for the deep plant-room excavation
planned beneath Block B of Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program. The excavation is a
rectangular pit approximately 68 ft × 44 ft in plan, cut into the podium footprint east of the shared Block A/B
basement. Excavation commences from a working grade at El. 750.0 and terminates at a plant-room subgrade at
El. 726.0, a total excavated depth of 24 ft.
The temporary works described herein are the Contractor's means and methods and are supplied by delegated
1.2 Selected System
A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
• (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
• (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
• (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
lagging.
Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

8.1  Consolidation of the Clay Aquitard
The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard is normally-consolidated (Section 5.2). Any net stress increase q applied at
the top of the clay will produce virgin, one-dimensional consolidation settlement along the Cc slope. In terms of
the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
Sc  = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]
with:
•  Cc = 0.28
•  e0 = 0.92
•  H (thickness of clay) = 18 ft
•  σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth of clay (El. 729)
For any q > (σ'p − σ'0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin compression governs and the above expression applies. Because σ'p is
only marginally above σ'0, this threshold is exceeded by essentially any structural or fill load of engineering
interest.

8.1  Consolidation of the Clay Aquitard
The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard is normally-consolidated (Section 5.2). Any net stress increase q applied at
the top of the clay will produce virgin, one-dimensional consolidation settlement along the Cc slope. In terms of
the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
Sc  = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]
with:
•  Cc = 0.28
•  e0 = 0.92
•  H (thickness of clay) = 18 ft
•  σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth of clay (El. 729)
For any q > (σ'p − σ'0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin compression governs and the above expression applies. Because σ'p is
only marginally above σ'0, this threshold is exceeded by essentially any structural or fill load of engineering
interest.
