arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import math

Ka1 = (1 - math.sin(math.radians(32))) / (1 + math.sin(math.radians(32)))
Ka2 = (1 - math.sin(math.radians(26))) / (1 + math.sin(math.radians(26)))
print(f"Ka1={Ka1:.4f}, Ka2={Ka2:.4f}")

# Effective vertical stresses:
# El 750: 250
# El 742: 250 + 8*118 = 1194
# El 738: 1194 + 4*(118-62.4) = 1416.4
# El 726: 1416.4 + 12*(120-62.4) = 2107.6
sv_750 = 250.0
sv_742 = 250.0 + 8.0 * 118.0
sv_738 = sv_742 + 4.0 * (118.0 - 62.4)
sv_726 = sv_738 + 12.0 * (120.0 - 62.4)
print("sv:", sv_750, sv_742, sv_738, sv_726)

# Use rounded Ka1=0.3073, Ka2=0.3905 as in Kesterline
Ka1_r = 0.3073
Ka2_r = 0.3905
pa_750 = Ka1_r * sv_750
pa_742 = Ka1_r * sv_742
pa_738_u = Ka1_r * sv_738
pa_738_l = Ka2_r * sv_738
pa_726 = Ka2_r * sv_726

# Trapezoid 1: 750 to 742 (h=8)
F1_rect = pa_750 * 8.0
z1_rect = 746.0
F1_tri = 0.5 * (pa_742 - pa_750) * 8.0
z1_tri = 742.0 + 8.0/3.0

# Trapezoid 2: 742 to 738 (h=4)
F2_rect = pa_742 * 4.0
z2_rect = 740.0
F2_tri = 0.5 * (pa_738_u - pa_742) * 4.0
z2_tri = 738.0 + 4.0/3.0

# Trapezoid 3: 738 to 726 (h=12)
F3_rect = pa_738_l * 12.0
z3_rect = 732.0
F3_tri = 0.5 * (pa_726 - pa_738_l) * 12.0
z3_tri = 726.0 + 12.0/3.0

forces = [(F1_rect, z1_rect), (F1_tri, z1_tri), (F2_rect, z2_rect), (F2_tri, z2_tri), (F3_rect, z3_rect), (F3_tri, z3_tri)]
P_soil = sum(f for f, z in forces)
M_soil = sum(f * (745.5 - z) for f, z in forces)
P_w = 0.5 * 62.4 * (16.0**2)
z_w = 726.0 + 16.0/3.0
M_w = P_w * (745.5 - z_w)
print(f"P_soil={P_soil:.1f}, M_soil={M_soil:.1f}, P_w={P_w:.1f}, M_w={M_w:.1f}")
print(f"Total P={P_soil+P_w:.1f}, Total M_D={M_soil+M_w:.1f}")
EOF

The verification of Package A Register **Item 048** (Kesterline Engineering, PC Support of Excavation Submittal `31-SH-B Rev.1`, sealed `06/11/2026`, as supplemented by Revision 2 Engineering Supplement `KE-L-2026-0713`, sealed `07/13/2026`) has been completed against the Package A project record. The verification memorandum addressed to **Rachel Marlbeck** has been issued on the Thelbridge memorandum form and saved to:

* **Deliverable Path:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx`

---

### 1. Basis of Review Applied
The review was conducted against the governing project record documents:
* **Geotechnical Investigation Report (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2`, `02/14/2025`), Boring Logs & Groundwater Monitoring Record (`B-01 to B-09`, Rounds 1–19 through `06/28/2026`), Field Observation Report (`KGI-FO-2026-0528`, `05/28/2026`), and Laboratory Index/Consolidation Data (`Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx`, `Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx`, `01/09/2025`):**
  * **Stratigraphy & Unit Weights at Block B (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §§5.2, 6.1–6.4, Tables 5-1 & 6-1):**
    * *Engineered Granular Fill (`SM` / `SP-SM`, placed `10/06/2025–11/02/2025`):* $\text{El. } 750.0\text{ to El. } 738.0$ ($12.0\text{ ft}$), $\gamma_{\text{total}} = 118\text{ pcf}$, $\phi' = 32^\circ$, $c' = 0$, $K_a = 0.3073$, $K_p = 3.25$.
    * *Compressible Clay Aquitard (`CL`, normally consolidated, $C_c = 0.28, e_0 = 0.92, \sigma'_p = 1,900\text{ psf}, k \approx 10^{-8}\text{ cm/s}$):* $\text{El. } 738.0\text{ to El. } 720.0$ ($18.0\text{ ft}$ total thickness; $6.0\text{ ft}$ residual clay plug below plant-room subgrade $\text{El. } 726.0$), $\gamma_{\text{total}} = 120\text{ pcf}$, drained $\phi' = 26^\circ, c' = 100\text{ psf}$ ($K_a = 0.3905, K_p = 2.56$), and **logged undrained shear strength $s_u = 900\text{ to } 1,100\text{ psf}$** (mean $1,000\text{ psf}$) from field vane and UU triaxial testing on companion Shelby-tube samples (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §6.3, p. 13).
    * *Confined Dense Sand & Gravel Aquifer (`SW-GW`):* Below $\text{El. } 720.0$ ($>60\text{ ft}$ thick), $\gamma_{\text{total}} = 130\text{ pcf}$, SPT refusal $N \ge 50\text{ blows}/6\text{ in}$.
  * **Logged Groundwater Regime (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §§7.1–7.3, Table 7-1; `KGI-FO-2026-0528` §§3–6):**
    * *Unconfined Shallow Phreatic Water Table:* **$\text{El. } 742.0\text{ ft}$** (logged range $\text{El. } 741.6\text{ to } 742.4\text{ ft}$ in standpipes `P-01`, `P-03`, `P-09` and Block A cut-face seepage at $\text{El. } 741.8\text{–}742.2\text{ ft}$).
    * *Confined Artesian Piezometric Head (`SW-GW` Aquifer below $\text{El. } 720.0$):* **$\text{El. } 738.0\text{ ft}$** ($18.0\text{ ft}$ of artesian head above the aquifer top at $\text{El. } 720.0\text{ ft}$; logged range $\text{El. } 737.7\text{ to } 738.3\text{ ft}$ in deep piezometers `P-04`/`B-04` inside the Block B plant-room footprint and `P-08`/`B-08` adjacent to the Block B mat, confirmed unaffected by Block A well-point dewatering or Block B fill/piling operations).
* **Design Basis Memorandum (`CB-DBM-001 Rev.2`, `11/14/2025`), Structural Drawings & Calculations (`Sheet S-101 Rev.4`, `Sheet S-201 Rev.4`, `CB-STR-011`, `CB-GEO-004`), Dewatering Plan (`Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1`, `06/04/2025`), and Specifications (`31 20 00 Rev.3`, `31 50 00`, `31 62 16`):**
  * Full hydrostatic water pressure ($\gamma_w = 62.4\text{ pcf}$) below $\text{El. } 742.0$ (`CB-DBM-001 Rev.2` §5.3);
  * Base-heave stability under ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6) counteracting dead-load factor $0.9D$ requiring $FS_{\text{heave}} = 0.9W / u \ge 1.50$ (`CB-DBM-001 Rev.2` §6.2; `KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §§8.2, 9.4);
  * Free-earth support rotational toe stability $FS_{\text{toe}} = M_R / M_D \ge 1.50$ (U.S. Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual / USACE EM 1110-2-2504);
  * Tieback anchor design and proof testing per `FHWA-IF-99-015` and `PTI DC35.1`;
  * Sheet-pile flexure per `AISC 360-16` Chapter F ($F_b = 0.60 F_y = 30.0\text{ ksi}$, $FS_{\text{flex}} \ge 1.50$) and lateral wall deflection $\delta_{\max} \le H/200 = 1.44\text{ in}$.

---

### 2. Summary of Technical Findings, Working, and Which Checks Can vs. Cannot Be Carried Forward

#### A. Checks That CAN Be Carried Forward as They Stand
1. **Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1, 3.3 (Stratigraphy Elevations & Unit Weights) and Sections 4.1, 4.2 ($250\text{ psf}$ Surcharge & $10\text{-ft}$ Equipment Exclusion):** The soil interfaces ($\text{El. } 750.0$, $\text{El. } 738.0$, $\text{El. } 726.0$, $\text{El. } 720.0$, $H = 24.0\text{ ft}$), total unit weights ($118 / 120 / 130\text{ pcf}$), and $250\text{ psf}$ surface surcharge match the project record.
2. **Supplement Section R2.1 & Part of R2.7 (Groundwater Basis, Active Relief-Well Depressurization Concept, $72\text{-hr}$ Hold & $\text{El. } 727.0$ Stop-Work Trigger — Contingent on Sealed Block B Dewatering Submittal):** Withdraws the invalid Rev.1 §3.4 dry-excavation assumption and specifies four $8\text{-in}$ relief wells (`RW-B1` to `RW-B4`, screened $\text{El. } 718.0\text{–}705.0$ in `SW-GW` with continuous annular bentonite-cement seal from $\text{El. } 721.0\text{ to } 738.0$ across the `CL` clay aquitard per `KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §9.6) pumped to maintain confined head $\le \text{El. } 726.5$ ($11.5\text{ ft}$ drawdown from $\text{El. } 738.0$), verified by three vibrating-wire piezometers (`VW-B1` to `VW-B3`, sensor tips at $\text{El. } 719.0$) with a mandatory $72\text{-hour}$ confirmation hold prior to excavating below $\text{El. } 732.0$ and an immediate stop-work trigger at $\text{El. } 727.0$.
3. **Supplement Section R2.2 (Excavation Base Heave Verification — Supersedes Rev.1 §5):**
   * Residual clay plug thickness below subgrade $\text{El. } 726.0$: $t_{\text{plug}} = 726.0 - 720.0 = 6.0\text{ ft}$.
   * Unfactored clay plug weight: $W = 6.0\text{ ft} \times 120\text{ pcf} = 720.0\text{ psf}$; factored resisting weight per `CB-DBM-001 Rev.2` §6.2: $0.9W = 648.0\text{ psf}$.
   * *Unpumped ($\text{El. } 738.0$, $h_w = 18.0\text{ ft}$):* $u = 18.0 \times 62.4 = 1,123.2\text{ psf} \implies FS_{\text{heave}} = 648.0 / 1,123.2 = 0.58 < 1.0$ (blowout failure).
   * *Depressurized ($\le \text{El. } 726.5$, $h_w = 6.5\text{ ft}$):* $u = 6.5 \times 62.4 = 405.6\text{ psf} \implies FS_{\text{heave}} = 648.0 / 405.6 = 1.60 \ge 1.50$ required (unfactored $W/u = 1.78$).
4. **Supplement Section R2.3 (Layered Effective-Stress + Hydrostatic Lateral Loading Above Subgrade — Supersedes Rev.1 §4.3 & §5):**
   * Total vertical stress at subgrade $\text{El. } 726.0$: $\sigma_{v0} = 250 + 12(118) + 12(120) = 3,106.0\text{ psf}$.
   * Effective vertical stress profile ($\sigma'_v$): $250.0\text{ psf}$ at $\text{El. } 750.0$; $1,194.0\text{ psf}$ at $\text{El. } 742.0$; $1,416.4\text{ psf}$ at $\text{El. } 738.0$; $2,107.6\text{ psf}$ at $\text{El. } 726.0$.
   * Integrating $p_a = K_a \sigma'_v$ ($K_{a1} = 0.3073$ for $\phi'=32^\circ$, $K_{a2} = 0.3905$ for $\phi'=26^\circ$, $c'=0$) yields horizontal soil force $P_{\text{soil}} = 11,622.8\text{ lb/ft}$ with resultant arm $10.681\text{ ft}$ below waler $\text{El. } 745.5$ ($\text{El. } 734.82$) and driving moment $M_{\text{soil}} = 124,141\text{ ft-lb/ft}$.
   * Hydrostatic pressure from $\text{El. } 742.0\text{ to El. } 726.0$ ($h_w = 16.0\text{ ft}$): $P_w = \frac{1}{2}(62.4)(16.0)^2 = 7,987.2\text{ lb/ft}$ acting at $\text{El. } 731.333$ (arm $14.167\text{ ft}$ below $\text{El. } 745.5$), giving $M_w = 113,152\text{ ft-lb/ft}$.
   * Total driving load above subgrade: $P_{\text{driv}} = 19,610.0\text{ lb/ft}$; total driving moment about anchor $\text{El. } 745.5$: $M_D = 237,293\text{ ft-lb/ft}$.
5. **Supplement Section R2.6 Allowable Section Capacity Only:** The allowable flexural capacity of the `PZ-35` Grade 50 section ($S_x = 48.5\text{ in}^3\text{/ft}$, $F_b = 0.60 F_y = 30.0\text{ ksi}$) is $M_{\text{allow}} = (30.0 \times 48.5)/12 = 121\text{ kip-ft/ft}$.

#### B. Checks That CANNOT Be Carried Forward as They Stand
1. **Rev.1 Section 3.2 (Undrained Shear Strength $s_u$) & Supplement Section R2.4 (Sheet-Pile Toe Embedment Check — FAILS):**
   * Kesterline uses an unverified undrained shear strength of **$s_u = 1,400\text{ psf}$** carried from Rev.1 §3.2 to compute net passive pressure $p_n = 4s_u - \sigma_{v0} = 4(1,400) - 3,106 = 2,494.0\text{ psf}$, $P_p = 2,494.0 \times 6.5 = 16,211\text{ lb/ft}$ over $D = 6.5\text{ ft}$ (tip $\text{El. } 719.5$, mid-embedment $\text{El. } 722.75$, arm $z_p = 22.75\text{ ft}$), $M_R = 368,800\text{ ft-lb/ft}$, and $FS_{\text{toe}} = 368,800 / 237,293 = 1.55 \ge 1.50$.
   * Against the **logged Geotechnical Report (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §6.3, p. 13) undrained shear strength $s_u = 900\text{ to } 1,100\text{ psf}$** (mean $1,000\text{ psf}$), the $6.5\text{ ft}$ embedment fails rotational stability across the entire logged strength range:
     * **At logged upper bound ($s_u = 1,100\text{ psf}$):** $p_n = 4(1,100) - 3,106 = 1,294.0\text{ psf}$; $P_p = 1,294.0 \times 6.5 = 8,411.0\text{ lb/ft}$; $M_R = 8,411.0 \times 22.75 = 191,350\text{ ft-lb/ft}$; **$FS_{\text{toe}} = 191,350 / 237,293 = 0.81 < 1.50$ (unstable, $FS < 1.0$)**.
     * **At logged mean ($s_u = 1,000\text{ psf}$):** $p_n = 4(1,000) - 3,106 = 894.0\text{ psf}$; $P_p = 894.0 \times 6.5 = 5,811.0\text{ lb/ft}$; $M_R = 5,811.0 \times 22.75 = 132,200\text{ ft-lb/ft}$; **$FS_{\text{toe}} = 132,200 / 237,293 = 0.56 < 1.50$ (unstable, $FS < 1.0$)**.

### 3. Effect of the Excavation Released by This Submittal on Permanent Work Already Built at Block B
Kesterline's design models the $68\text{ ft} \times 44\text{ ft}$ Block B plant-room excavation (`Grids H–L / 3–5`) as an open greenfield cut from working grade $\text{El. } 750.0$ to subgrade $\text{El. } 726.0$, asserting in Rev.1 §4.4 that no permanent structures lie within the $1\text{H}:1\text{V}$ or $1.5H$ ($36\text{ ft}$) influence zone. Against the as-built record, releasing this excavation would severely impact permanent work already constructed at Block B:
1. **Cutting Through and Undermining the As-Built Block A/B Reinforced Concrete Basement Mat (`Sheet S-101 Rev.4`, `Sheet S-201 Rev.4`, `CB-STR-011`, Register Item 050):** The continuous $3.0\text{-ft}$-thick reinforced concrete basement mat ($\text{underside El. } 731.5$, $\text{top El. } 734.5$, over $3\text{-in}$ lean concrete blinding) covers `Grids B–L / 1–5` across both Block A and Block B and was cast on `01/12/2026` (with Level-2 slabs cast `05/18/2026–06/05/2026` and the Level-3 slab cage staged for `07/22/2026`). Because the plant-room footprint (`Grids H–L / 3–5`) lies inside the Block B mat footprint, driving sheets from $\text{El. } 750.0$ and excavating to $\text{El. } 726.0$ would require cutting/demolishing the completed $3.0\text{-ft}$ permanent mat, breaching the below-grade waterproofing and waterstop continuity (`Sheet A-501`, `Detail 4/S-201`), and excavating $5.5\text{ ft}$ below the mat underside ($\text{El. } 731.5\text{ to El. } 726.0$) without underpinning or surcharge design.
2. **Exposing, Unbracing, and Undermining 16 of the 48 As-Built Permanent Driven Pipe Piles (`Pile_Installation_Records_BlockB.xlsx`, `Sheet S-101 Rev.4`, `Detail 2/S-201`):** All 48 permanent $16\text{-in OD} \times 0.500\text{-in}$ wall ASTM A252 Grade 3 closed-end pipe piles (`P-1` to `P-48`, $180\text{ kips}$ service load) were driven from $\text{El. } 750.0$ between `11/06/2025` and `11/21/2025` to tips at $\text{El. } 686.0\text{–}690.0$, with pile cutoffs at $\text{El. } 732.5$ and pile caps from $\text{El. } 732.0\text{ to El. } 734.5$. Sixteen ($16$) of those 48 permanent piles ($4\text{ rows along Grids H, J, K, L} \times 4\text{ piles/row between Grids 3 and 5}$) lie directly inside the plant-room excavation footprint. Excavating to $\text{El. } 726.0$ removes all $12.0\text{ ft}$ of engineered fill ($\text{El. } 750.0\text{–}738.0$, placed `10/06/2025–11/02/2025`) and the upper $12.0\text{ ft}$ of the `CL` clay aquitard ($\text{El. } 738.0\text{–}726.0$) — $24.0\text{ ft}$ of soil confinement — around those 16 piles, cuts $6.5\text{ ft}$ below their cutoff elevation ($\text{El. } 732.5$) and $6.0\text{ ft}$ below their pile cap undersides ($\text{El. } 732.0$), and leaves the upper pile shafts freestanding and laterally unbraced against buckling.
3. **De-Rating Certified Pile Axial Capacity (`CB-GEO-004`):** EOR calculation `CB-GEO-004` certified $Q_{\text{ult}} = 480\text{ kips}$ ($Q_{\text{all}} = 240\text{ kips}$ at $FS = 2.0$ vs. $180\text{ kips}$ service load) by crediting $Q_{s,\text{upper}} = 85\text{ kips}$ of positive shaft resistance between $\text{El. } 750.0$ and $\text{El. } 720.0$ ($10\text{ kips}$ in the $12\text{ ft}$ fill plus $75\text{ kips}$ in the $18\text{ ft}$ clay). Excavating to $\text{El. } 726.0$ physically removes the entire $12\text{ ft}$ fill ($10\text{ kips}$) and $12\text{ ft}$ of the $18\text{ ft}$ clay ($\frac{12}{18} \times 75 = 50\text{ kips}$), directly stripping **$60\text{ kips/pile}$** of upper shaft capacity (and unloading $\sigma'_v$ in the underlying `SW-GW` bearing stratum by $1,857.6\text{ psf}$, reducing $Q_{s,\text{lower}}$), even before accounting for clay consolidation downdrag under Register Item 049.
4. **Tieback Clashes, Lateral Soil Movement ($p\text{-}y$) on Adjacent Piles, and Aquitard Short-Circuiting:** Installing $49\text{+ ft}$ tiebacks at $6\text{ ft}$ centers outward from `Grids H–L / 3–5` risks physical collision with adjacent permanent $16\text{-in}$ pipe piles (`Grid G` and perimeter lines); lateral wall deflection ($\ge 1.3\text{ in}$) imposes unanalyzed lateral displacements on the adjacent pile group and basement mat; and the 16 pile shafts penetrating the residual $6.0\text{ ft}$ clay plug require aquitard collar seals per `KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` §9.6.
